A Time of War: A Memoir Across Three Generations

Dear reader, it is with great excitement that I offer this expansive work for your consideration: A recently unearthed, voluminous manuscript – an epic memoir written over the course of three generations. It is a work as monumental and daunting as it is groundbreaking - a glimpse into the inner workings of the true scientific mind.

Upon discovery of these immaculate pages, I, suffering great personal expense, set forth to ensure the general publication and distribution of this important history. It is a work that will perhaps elucidate upon and justify the eccentric reputations of my forebears.

While I admit that I am biased in this appraisal, as it is my own exemplary lineage which is documented, I submit this comprehensive prosopography in as accurate a condition as I can muster. As one will soon attest, it is a chronicle of events of a decidedly fantastical nature, yet my research confirms it to be as true and vital a work as has ever been seen in print.

However, I must offer a word of caution to those with weaker constitutions. While these pages hold a brilliant catalogue of achievements, they also boldly depict the setbacks encountered along the journey. Gruesome, grim, and horrifying as they may be, I have included their spine-chilling contents as originally written. As one might expect, in exposing the base components of the universe, we uncover both light and darkness in equal measure. For without darkness, we cannot appreciate the brilliance of the light.
Taking Sides

My father was a genius! I state this now, not with the naïveté of my initial discovery of his journal, but as a time-tested statement of truth. It is why I pen these words today for posterity and to affirm with deep conviction what some may erroneously refer to as mad science.

When I first arrived at my father's manor, I carried the same skepticism any normal individual would. Weary as I was from the excursion across the Hungarian plains, the cold, gray walls of the villa with its oppressive iron gates chilled me to my marrow. When the disfigured caretaker — the only person privileged with the knowledge — revealed to me a false door and spiraling staircase that descended to a secret laboratory, the grim discovery did nothing to soothe my nerves. In fact, the sight of jars filled with preserved flesh and the astringent stench of chemicals aggravated my frail state, leaving me to take my suppers in the bedroom for several weeks.

But, it was this same dark discovery that eventually roused me from my illness. For as I pored over the journal bequeathed to me and surveyed page after page of formulaic experimentation, my apprehensions melted. I felt trepidacious, yet unreservedly enthusiastic at the ethical implications of this great task!

Yet even after the disquiet within my soul was relieved, the nearby village rattled my window panes with cacophonous revelry. At first, I kept my visits to the borough brief and infrequent. It seemed that whenever I turned my head I would lock eyes with a cautious observer, and I felt the entire town's steel gaze like daggers tickling the back of my skull. I could only speculate that my siblings endured the same sordid treatment.

It was my spouse, using my extended rest to become better acquainted with the village, who explained how spirited political discourse was the source of this commotion. Then I could discern the rally cry of their evening demonstrations as they spoke of disobedience, the end of monarchy, and civil war.

I began to realize the potential boon that war could provide for my research. If the people shared a mere fraction of the passion that now stoked the fires of my heart, how easily they would embrace my scientific assistance! While my father's ambitions were strong, his solitary existence had doomed his ideas to obscurity.

I would not repeat this error. I would brave the jeers of the populace to guide them in the art of warfare. My efforts would determine the course of this conflict. And when the time comes, it will be my science that will emerge from the flames of war as the true victor!
War on the Horizon

The spectre of war haunted the small village. This ideological tension would erupt in loud displays and gatherings of the peasantry near the Town Hall. For all the folderol, I began to cherish the moments when the eerie stillness of the evening was broken by anguished yells.

The Separatists felt alienated by the aristocratic government and wished to secede. Their brash tactics aimed to incite a democratic revolt among the proletariat. The Unified Monarchists feared the anarchic destabilization of the economy at such a key moment during industrialization. I was quickly able to determine that the town supported the {{0=...|Separatists|...}}.

Plagued by Conflict

If one can call the prospect of perpetual conflict stabilizing, my life settled into a somewhat steady routine. During the day, the sound of distant gunfire rumbled through the halls of my estate as silver plumes of smoke billowed beyond the mountainous horizon, casting tendril-like shadows across the land — a constant reminder of civil war. At night, the rare spectacle of an explosion brightening the sky surprised me with how viscerally I reacted.

Soldiers in their bright regalia keep watch over the town from a newly erected outpost, waving the brilliant orange flag of royalty. The Monarchy had claimed victory from afar after stationing their ranks across the region, but as scuffles remained constant, this declaration was all pomp without substance. The Monarchy drafted citizens into their ranks and levied penalties against those who showed disloyalty.

The inference that one of my standing should owe a debt of servitude to those who already tax my earnings into oblivion was enough to make me spill my tea. And to what end, I wondered? Could peace be mustered in a populace kept so distant from the individuals who ruled it? It was called the industrial revolution for a reason, was it not?

But, I must admit, the safety that the Monarchy afforded appealed to my pocketbook. Appeasing the Monarchy would ensure money and influence, but it also appeared — for better or ill — that royalty was distant enough to take little interest in our experimentations unless they provided direct benefit to themselves, whereas the Separatists were interested in knowledge and were desperate to explore all scientific options available to them to turn the tide. However, their frail sensibilities would not so easily accept my experimentations.

Ah, to be left to one's own devices or to be famously scrutinized, reviled, and revered in equal measure! The decision weighed upon me so heavily it gave me mild indigestion during my evening banquets. What direction should I choose to advance my most important scientific work?
Down with the Monarchy

The length and difficulty of my journey was exacerbated by the ongoing conflict. Compounding this harried inconvenience, my spouse and I suffered the indignity of a lengthy interrogation by soldiers of the Separatist forces, who had imposed an unofficial martial government.

Peasants-turned-soldiers in their motley uniforms keep watch over the town from a newly erected outpost waving a sanguine flag. They spoke of freedom as they dug fresh graves in the cemetery - the wrought iron gates perpetually wreathed in lilies. I observed the daily horse-drawn carts, dragging the wounded towards ill-equipped infirmaries - my crimson reflection in the muddy ruts of unpaved highways.

It was both in spite of and because of this brashness that I found myself drawn to the scrappy Separatist upstarts and their eagerness to fight for the capricious whims of the great unwashed. The Separatists were desperate for the advantages that my family's experimentations provided, and while hesitant over our methods, were willing to further our knowledge in return. Unfortunately, this relationship made them more entitled to levy accusations towards us.

However, the influence of the throne was still absolute. If one could ingratiate themselves with the distracted Monarchy, their influence and money was on offer. The peasantry would be too discontent to focus on our more "ambitious" works. Unfortunately, unless experimentation directly benefited them, the Monarchy had no use for it.

Ah, to be left to one's own devices or to be famously scrutinized, reviled, and revered in equal measure! The decision weighed upon me so heavily that I could scarcely enjoy my afternoon pastries. Neither could the muffled wailing coming from the cellar laboratory nor the distant clattering of gunfire at night calm my weary mind. What direction should I choose to advance my most important scientific work?
Seeds of Conflict

Before my spouse and I had even settled our affairs, I was rewarded not only for my family's numerous contributions to the region, but also for the political allegiance I held (or dreadfully inherited as the case may be). Further promises of considerable clout were made if I were to continue to support the war.

As the conflict raged on, it was clear that with my business acumen, noble influence, and burgeoning scientific genius, I would be a highly sought after ally.

I was quick to suggest a few "enhancements" to their battery and presented several advanced weaponry schematics which could prove instrumental to victory.

While the rumors of my parent's eccentricities made them hesitant, the promise of support from my lucrative estate proved too much to resist. If I could demonstrate to them the visceral efficacy of my proposal, they promised further investment. An easy task.

Emboldened by their conquest of a royal power and enlivened with pride in their country, this righteous fervor became a frenzy. A Modern Future
While the discovery of my family's experiments and journals would cement my scientific ambitions for years to come, I had never actually met them. I was too young to remember the disappearance of my brilliant progenitor. To lose a parent and then another to the subsequent dementia that followed was more folly than one child should ever have to bear. I was shielded from this reality, rushed away to Vienna, where I was consumed by my studies until my twenty-first year. It was only at my partner's insistence that I decided to settle my inheritance.

I remember being stunned as I arrived by train on a mid-summer's evening. I do not know what I expected from the anecdotes my nanny had relayed to me, but it was not the bustling cityscape that greeted me. As the sun dipped into the forest, the glimmer of modern steel light fixtures amplified the urban luminescence. My delighted spouse and I enjoyed a quiet ride in our steamer car which offered us a chance to observe the idyllic community and decidedly pleasant folk enjoying the convenience of electricity and steam turbine technology.

The estate appeared untouched by years of vacancy - recently pruned brambles and ivy adorned the iron gate and the expansive grounds were immaculate. A caretaker of great age and a small housekeeping staff greeted us. Although updating the grounds to the more modern standard of the nearby town would prove a daunting task, the servants’ warm reception allayed our remaining anxieties. Upon discovery of my family's laboratory, what had been planned as a mere visit received an indefinite extension.

However, when I spoke of my family's history of experimentation, I was rarely met with indifference but more often firm words of encouragement. It appeared that this region, so rife with abnormal progress, viewed my theories as rudimentary but delightfully avant-garde. Even when I expounded upon dark rituals and the grotesque, they encouraged further exploration and referred me to the newly constructed University.

This caused me severe consternation. Was this not what I wanted — a clear path towards scientific enlightenment and support of my family's landmark ideas? Why did their lack of friction vex me so? Did they view my illustrious work as trivial?

It was this grim realization that strengthened my will. If these craven modernists wanted more, then so be it! I would push the limits of science further than ever before and damn the consequences!

English_Source: New Science

When I discovered the journal, the masterwork plans, and the clandestine fragments of experiments in the laboratory, I laughed. Surely, my great-grandfather had grandiose ambitions at the time, but modern advancements made many of the blueprints obsolete and frankly, a bit cute.

I decided to improve upon them, and I knew just the thing that would dazzle them all!
Rediscovered Artist

An art critic arrived at my estate, and immediately took an enthusiastic interest in the misshapen wooden figure.

He explained his theory on the authenticity of the artistic piece: "His more well-known work in marble defined most of his career, however we believe that Ferenczy explored an abstract modernist period well before his contemporaries, with wooden figures."

The collector offered me $2 for the misshapen wooden figure, a sum that I gladly accepted in order to be rid of the hideous thing.
The Key

I noticed that the misshapen wooden figure felt hollow inside. With a moment's hesitation, I cracked the object against the corner of the table. The contents spilled out upon the floor.

The object inside could not exist, and yet there it was. My mind was filled with questions that I knew might never be fully answered, but I was thankful for the assistance.
Time Machine - Publication?

While the ideas set forth in my parent's journal entries were both outdated and embarrassingly rudimentary in some areas, one thing that the fools in academia hounded us to provide was the schematics to the Time Conveyance Device. For a discovery so radical and immense in its influence on multiple dimensions of the world, the meager sums they offered for entrusting it to their universities was insulting.

I would never give it to them to abuse secretly at their discretion. No! But to publish it widely and allow all of the Hungarian people the chance to rewrite history? That, it seemed, would be the sort of experimental chaos the stuffed shirts at the university would never see coming!

But, perhaps, and most undoubtably, it would have untold repercussions.

The issue at hand, however, was the matter of secrecy. If any one of us - myself or my dear cousins - decided to publish the schematic, it would be freely available.

I knew that each would need to make their own private decision and I prayed that it would be the correct choice.
Fate of Time

I was called upon to make my choice between secrecy and the unknown.

If I chose to focus on Utopian Experiments and conceal the time machine, the townspeople may be slightly harder to please, but I would ensure stability and have time to devise a new schematic.

However, if I were the only one to release the time machine schematics, I would receive extra glory. This choice would definitely cause a completely random special event to occur. It might be really good, really terrible, or somewhere in between.

The decision was easy. We should:

Focus on Utopian Experiments and keep the schematics hidden.

Release the Time Machine schematics to the general public.
{{0=?|A Bend Towards Chaos|A Secure Future}}

To hell with academia! I was not afraid of some minor fourth-dimensial tampering. Would it not be immoral to refuse all persons the basic human right to alter their own fate? I would unlock and disperse the secrets of creation no matter what horrors lay before me.

Publishing the means to construct a time machine to the general public was a calculated move that even the most daring polymath wouldn't be brave enough to make. My family would leave an indelible mark on the timeline of the cosmos regardless of the anarchic course that now lay ahead.

Bold as it would have been to openly allow the public to source parts and make their own journey through time, the potential time loss was too great to ignore. With the future already at my fingertips, there was no need to ride the waves of chaos. With the precision of a potter molding clay at the wheel, I would design a perfect world.
Because of our decision, the town has seen the brilliance of our vision and will honor the best amongst us appropriately with a special monument.
The Consequences of Free Time Travel

The fools! The absolute imbeciles! The diabolical currs! My cousins knew there could be dire consequences for allowing time travel to become accessible to almost anyone, and now I would be forced to abide the random effects of a force unknown.
Click to create a new paradox!
{{0=|A Surge of Productivity|A Clarity of Purpose|None Left Behind|Future Notes|Trust and Benevolence|A Return to Suspicion|Targeted|Utter Catastrophe}}

The time device proved to be invaluable for productivity. While the general populace squabbled over self-interests, creating and destroying the countryside in equal measure with varying degrees of incalculable existential horror, I was generally left to my leisure in solitude with my spouse and servants.

One flick of an electrical switch and the copper fixtures of the device sent me back to the moments before a failed experiment. I soon became acquainted with visitations from myself, even sharing tea with several versions of my person to talk over and revise a particularly difficult thesis. While the process aged me quicker than desired, the ingredients it saved and the excellent conversation proved well worth it.

Technological advancement retrieved from the future, the stability offered by knowing you can change your past, the ability to travel backwards in time to guide one's self away from a rough day ahead - general access to a time machine could lift a near Utopia right to the edge of perfection!

While I was somewhat disappointed in the lack of chaos, I was ecstatic at the reaction of the university elite. Our decision had such a positive effect on the world, it made the academics positively seethe! Those furrowed brows and anxious worry lines grafted onto their imbecilic faces made the outcome of this rash decision a joy to behold. It wasn't long before this joy gave way to clarity of purpose. I felt reinvigorated, hoping each day that my next experiment would evoke the same horrific response.

If I were to forgo humility for a moment and describe one of my most favorable traits, I am a creature of infinite patience. So, I watched as the first experiments in time alteration bore miniscule results and continued in my tasks without paying them much heed. Like all initial fascinations, the wave of interest in manipulating fate slowly gave way to other technological distractions and time machines became popular children's toys around the holidays.

I cannot recollect the moment when I noticed it, perhaps it happened naturally, but as the timeline shifted ever so slowly, it appeared that the forces aligning the cosmos preferred stasis over the whims of chaos. With each passing season, the studious gap between myself and my cousins seemed to edge ever closer.

And though I abhorred the thought of intervention from forces outside of my understanding, I cannot say that I did not relish my stoicism being rewarded.

There are narrative consequences for unleashing a Time Machine into the wild, and the devastation is too far-reaching for one single paragraph in a mad scientist's memoir to detail. However, it has no effect on gameplay and therefore will be omitted.

It is better to write these words now in anticipation of the game, My Father's Work, which will see release in 2022 and detail the historical events of my family. I've played it a few times during my travels and while I wish it had a solo version, it's still very good.

Perhaps history will no longer align with the narrative presented in the game and this paragraph will seem oddly out of place. Ah, such is the confounding nature of time travel.

The people have developed a sense of trust and acceptance for my work after the unmitigated success of the time altering apparatus. Trust and acceptance? I grapple with this concept with many of my waking hours. Even on the days where I feel emboldened to venture backwards into the timestream to undo this stomach-turning adoration, some peon in the village simply undoes my work.

My beautifully macabre estate is now looked upon with exuberance by tourists to the region. Tourists! By god, this will make pushing the boundaries of ethical imagination nearly impossible! I must break through this irrational barrier of love and generosity before it stifles my work!

How could they accuse us of sedition? The Time Machine was my family's gift to all of humanity and yet they call it willfully negligent and unethical!

Do we blame Prometheus for every home burnt to the ground because of the invention of fire? Is the zoetrope responsible for every detestable piece of film created after it? Should we ban perfumes and colognes for their ability to more fervently entice couples into intimacy? It is only natural that the most important discoveries carry with them a modicum of insidious potential.

It is absurd that a correlative effect is so readily pinned upon me. Yet, their superstitions have once again returned!

They discovered who did it. Hungarian government tracked it.

Perhaps it was easy to discern this information as every pamphlet, editorial, journal, and detailed blueprint was signed in bold ink. It was all for naught as well. The Hungarian government quietly tracked each copy down with the assistance of the scientific community, and secured this knowledge for themselves alone.

My family's decision to disseminate this information had dire consequences for those that chose this path. Their Masterwork was rendered pointless to complete as it would be confiscated immediately by police force emboldened by access to the time stream. Fortunately, those that decided to remain silent could not be implicated merely by association and remained free to continue their work.

There is always a cycle of destruction and renewal with every major epoch in the world's history, and this would probably be seen as a minor stumbling block in the overall chronology of events. With the ease of general access to a device that had the power to bend time and space around it, it was soon discovered that the average individual may have lacked the self-control and intelligence required to prevent the catastrophic destruction of nearly every living thing in Eastern Europe.

Owning an Estate made of stone, looming high above the valley, I was able to retain most of my possessions. Although the air was now tinged with a hint of sulfur and resources were a touch harder to procure.

This was a minor setback.

This is not the end - it is only the beginning. My own story still remains to be written, forged into legacy like those before me. I will not stop until the sun is blotted out by the sheer heftiness of my imagination!
THE END?

My close friends and family - many of whom I have permanently severed contact with because of their feelings on the matter - have expressed extreme misgivings about the publication of this book. They claim that my macabre fascination with exposing this to the world is unhealthy!

Some have even derisively labeled this work as pseudoscience, homeopathy, or a drug-induced fever dream, but I say to them, "who are you to criticize the moon and the stars for being in the sky?" This work is important! How can they not see it? If anything, these outlandish experiments further prove the relevance of the science that is far better researched, performed, and peer-reviewed after publication in respected journals.

For while the world may have sped onward at a pace that our scientific contributions could not match, rendering our innovations lame and timid in comparison, I believe that my family's failure to make an impact on a world of the future is an important lesson. Our contributions must be remembered, not for their value to the progress of mankind, but for laying the foundations of the work that others would ignore because of other more viable innovations which they could hone to perfection.

The world may have progressed beyond a need for mad science, but I believe it is this spirit that will define my family's legacy. Even if what they did, does not.

The astute reader may have already surmised that the recollections of three generations was at many points noticeably vivid and detailed. Almost as if the author were not simply transcribing those moments from memory, but witnessing them first-hand. If not, then perhaps I am not as adept at my writing craft as I give myself credit.

Does it not seem peculiar that an individual from {{1=...|Testville|...}}, a small town in Eastern Europe, would become a household name at such a pace? Quite peculiar indeed, isn't it?

For you see, it was I, {{0=...|Anna|...}}, editor, author, and compiler of my family's illustrious personal memoir. This was not a memoir as proposed, but a non-fiction chronicle of events witnessed directly by myself. Being gifted a schematic of a Time Machine certainly has its benefits.

I will not attempt to persuade you to the authenticity of my account. With all the wondrous occurrences and graphic failures described within this lengthy tome - that I'm sure my family would never have admitted to of their own volition - I have no doubt that this revelation carries with it more credibility.
